extracted.intended_audience: general readers, policymakers, tribal leaders, and legal scholars interested in federal-tribal consultation policy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and historical/critical summary of Executive Order 13175 requiring federal agencies to consult and coordinate with Indian tribal governments when considering policies that affect tribal communities. Covers the order's substantive principles, agency obligations (planning, staffing, OMB review), enforcement limits, and criticisms/examples of noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal departments and agencies must consult with Indian tribal governments when considering policies that would impact tribal communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as the central provision of EO 13175; the majority of the order focuses on the imperative of incorporating tribal input into policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge unique government-to-government relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 13175 reiterates that the United States maintains a unique relationship with tribes as dependent nations and reaffirms tribal self-government, sovereignty, and self-determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a normative baseline for agency behavior and underpins the consultation obligation; rooted in treaties and longstanding federal Indian policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Afford tribal governments maximum discretion in implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should afford tribal governments maximum discretion in implementing federal policies within their communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positioned as one of the standards of behavior agencies must follow when developing and implementing policies anticipated to significantly impact tribes; implies deference to tribal choices about local implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default to tribal authority when feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: When feasible, federal agencies should default to tribal authority in matters affecting tribal communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the order's behavioral standards and consistent with respect for tribal sovereignty; functions as an instruction to prioritize tribal governance options where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in regular and meaningful consultation throughout policy development
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must engage in "regular and meaningful consultation with tribal leadership throughout the policy development process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order uses the phrase 'regular and meaningful' but does not define timing, format, or frequency; the lack of specificity has been criticized as contributing to inconsistent and ineffective consultation in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must develop coordination proposals and submit to OMB
rubrics_metrics.description: EO 13175 requests that all federal agencies and departments develop proposals for how they plan to coordinate with tribal governments and submit these plans to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural requirement intended to make agency consultation plans explicit and subject to executive-branch review; lack of follow-through has been cited as a compliance gap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appoint a staff member responsible for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency or department is directed to appoint a staff member responsible for ensuring compliance with Executive Order 13175.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an internal point of contact/accountability within agencies for tribal consultation obligations; absence of clear staffing has been linked to inconsistent implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation is not judicially enforceable / no private right of action
rubrics_metrics.description: The consultation requirement in EO 13175 is not judicially enforceable because it depends on the trust responsibility outlined in the Constitution rather than a statutory mandate, and the order explicitly states that it is not intended to create a private cause of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes that executive orders are typically unenforceable unless tied to a statutory mandate or private cause of action; this legal limitation affects the practical force of the EO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of specificity about timing, format, and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: While the order states that consultation should be 'regular and meaningful,' it does not clarify at what point in the policy development process consultation should take place, what communication format should be used, or how often consultation should take place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This vagueness is flagged as a key reason for inconsistent compliance; critics argue agencies need clearer standards (when to consult, how to document consultation, what constitutes adequacy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical/anti-pattern example: consultation after decisions and incomplete disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of the Interior's 2003 proposed reorganization (creating a Bureau for Indian Education Programs) impacted tribes but did not involve consultation during development; tribal input occurred only after public pressure, and the later consultation did not include a complete explanation of proposed changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an illustrative failure of EO 13175: consulting only after key decisions are made, providing incomplete information, and failing to consider tribal concerns in advance. Highlights what 'ineffective consultation' looks like in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive-branch follow-up requirement (Obama memorandum: 90-day plans)
rubrics_metrics.description: President Obama's 2009 'Memorandum on Tribal Consultation' required each federal agency or department to submit a plan within 90 days detailing their cooperation with Executive Order 13175.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents an administrative attempt to bolster compliance by setting a near-term deadline for agencies to produce concrete plans; also implicitly acknowledges prior inconsistent adherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation as part of the federal trust responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea that consultation is part of the federal government's trust responsibility to tribes is reiterated as a conceptual foundation for EO 13175.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames consultation as not merely good practice but connected to historic legal/political obligations; however, the EO's reliance on the trust relationship rather than statute affects enforceability.
